col.title: Title
detail.contained_body: a kill term matched inside a longer role name. Check this before trusting the kill.
detail.gaps_none: Your evidence covers every stated requirement.
detail.not_checked_body: the description was truncated or silent on this. Treated as unknown, never as a failure.
draft.never_sends: Dawnlist never sends. You send it yourself.
draft.send_ready: Ready to send from your mail app
families.armed_now: {name} is armed. Matching roles there will be screened out for nothing.
families.body: When you reject two roles of the same kind at one employer, Dawnlist offers a rule: kill that function at that employer, but keep reading the others. Nothing is armed until you say so, and every proposal shows the rejections it was built from.
families.heading: Employers you have turned down
families.none: Nothing proposed yet. These appear once you have rejected two similar roles at the same employer.
families.stood_down: {name} stood down. Nothing there is screened out by it now.
funnel.screen_drift: your screening rules removed {now}% of postings this run, against {before}% last run — check the rules if that was not intended
menu.language_changed: Dawnlist will be in {language} the next time you open it.
onboarding.aim_placeholder: A sentence or two, in your own words. What kind of role, roughly what level, where, permanent or contract, and the lowest salary worth a conversation. Anything you leave out, Dawnlist has to guess at.
onboarding.answer_placeholder: Your answer — leave blank if you would rather not say
onboarding.answers_added: {count} response(s) added to your background record above.
onboarding.answers_none: Nothing new to add — type an answer first.
onboarding.calibration_body: Here are ten live postings, with what Dawnlist made of each one. Correct anything it got wrong. Where you disagree, tell it what sentence would have got it right — that sentence goes into your brief, so the same mistake is not made again tomorrow.
onboarding.calibration_skipped: There were not enough live postings to calibrate against, so this step has been skipped — nothing you did. Dawnlist will calibrate on a morning when a search is switched on and the feed is reachable. You can finish setting up.
onboarding.disagreement: You disagree — Dawnlist said {app}, you say {user}.
onboarding.draft_failed: Could not draft from your CVs: {reason}. You can write both documents yourself and continue.
onboarding.drafted: Drafted. Correct anything that is wrong before continuing.
onboarding.drop_hint: Drop your CV files here — PDF, Word or plain text
onboarding.factsheet_label: Background factsheet — what may be said
onboarding.interview_body: Dawnlist has read your CVs and drafted two documents. Correct them — they are a starting point, not a verdict. The factsheet on the left is the only thing your outreach is allowed to claim about you. The brief on the right decides what gets surfaced each morning.
onboarding.low_signal: You agreed with everything, which usually means this sample was easy rather than that the brief is finished.
onboarding.open_questions: Dawnlist could not tell, and has left these open:
onboarding.ready: Ready — your brief will be updated with what you taught it.
onboarding.searches_body: These were suggested from what you said you are looking for. They start switched off, because each one costs money per posting it returns — so switch on the ones that are real searches, and leave the rest. You can change them at any time in Settings.
onboarding.searches_none: No searches were suggested. You can add them in Settings once you are set up.
onboarding.searches_off: Nothing is switched on, so tomorrow morning will be quiet. You can carry on and switch one on later in Settings.
onboarding.sentence_placeholder: What sentence, added to your brief, would have got this right?
onboarding.title: Dawnlist — setting up
rules.body: Before anything is read by a model, Dawnlist screens it against these terms. A posting killed here costs nothing; a posting that gets through costs a fraction of a penny to read. Start with none — add a term when you notice yourself making the same decision twice.
rules.conflict: Not added — this would have hidden a role you pursued:
rules.contextual_help: Words that mean something in a job title and nothing in a benefits paragraph. Matched against the title and company only.
rules.employers_help: Earned, not typed. Pursuing a role adds its employer here, and every later posting from them is read. Change the decision and it leaves again.
rules.heading: Screening rules
rules.strong_help: Signal anywhere — title, company or description. A posting matching one of these is always sent to be assessed.
rules.unsupported_help: Title terms that rule a posting out however good the employer. Checked first, and against every role you have pursued before it is accepted.
searches.body: These are the searches swept each morning. A search that is switched on costs money every day it runs, because the job feed bills per posting returned — so the ones Dawnlist suggested from what you told it start switched off until you have read them.
searches.heading: What Dawnlist looks for
searches.placeholder: a job title to look for
searches.switched_off: {label} is off. Nothing will be fetched for it.
searches.switched_on: {label} is on. It will be swept each morning.
settings.admin_body: Issue override codes, and withdraw them. A code grants access; it never sells anything. Say who each one is for — an unlabelled code cannot be accounted for later. A code meant for an app reviewer must allow several uses: a reviewer may test on more than one machine, or re-test after a rejection, and a spent code turns that into a failed review.
settings.admin_issued: Issued {code}. Copy it now; it is shown once here.
settings.admin_no_licence: No licence on this machine, so there is nothing to administer.
settings.admin_revoked: {code} withdrawn. It stops working on the next attempt.
settings.admin_uses_tip: How many times this code may be redeemed. Never 1 for a reviewer.
settings.code_redeemed: Code accepted — your licence is saved.
settings.data_body: Job postings in Dawnlist are licensed from a third-party data provider. You can use them for your own job search, including keeping the ones you shortlist. You may not redistribute or resell them, or use them to build a competing job service. These limits continue to apply to postings you keep after your subscription ends.
settings.data_heading: Where the job postings come from
settings.key_body: Dawnlist reads job postings and drafts your messages using Anthropic's models, on your own account. Create a key at console.anthropic.com and paste it here. You can revoke it at any time, and Dawnlist stores it in your operating system's credential manager — never in a file.
settings.key_forgotten: Key removed. Dawnlist cannot run until you add another.
settings.key_none: No key stored yet — Dawnlist cannot run without one.
settings.licence_body: Paste the licence key from your purchase email. If you were given an override code instead, paste that — Dawnlist will exchange it for a licence.
settings.report_body: Dawnlist uses generative AI to judge postings and to draft your messages. If it produces something inappropriate, offensive or plainly wrong, report it and it will be read.
settings.subscribe_body: Dawnlist's job feed is a subscription, bought through the App Store. Everything already on this Mac stays open either way — your board, your brief and your tracker do not need a subscription to read.
settings.subscribe_code_placeholder: Access code, if you were given one
settings.subscribe_done: Subscribed. The feed reads for you from tomorrow morning.
settings.subscribe_still_waiting: The App Store has not answered yet. If no purchase sheet appeared, check that you are signed in to the App Store — for a test build, under System Settings, App Store, Sandbox Account. You can try again, restore an earlier purchase, or carry on and subscribe later.
settings.subscribe_unavailable: The App Store cannot take a purchase on this Mac right now.
settings.title: Dawnlist — settings
update.body: This copy came from the website, so updates arrive from there too. The download page has the new version, signed, with its checksum published beside it. Nothing on this machine changes until you install it yourself.
update.title: Update available
voice.no_profile: No tone profile yet — add some of your own sent emails
voice.profile_from: Tone learned from {count} of your own sent messages
